process_area.title: In-Store Customer Safety Operations & Hazard Control

value_stream.name: Customer Safety, Premises Liability & In-Store Risk Management

fields.Participants: Store Ops (VS-07), HSE (VS-24), Stock Associates, IFM (VS-138), Customer Safety
fields.Trigger: Store open; shift change; scheduled cycle

workflows.name: Daily Store Safety Inspection, Hazard Hunt & Housekeeping

Automation Opportunity: - Hazard-driven mobile checklist; photo capture; auto-task to IFM/HSE; repeat-hazard analytics
Controls: - CTL-672: documented daily walk vs hazard register; immediate-hazard correction; findings logged incl. near-miss; trends reviewed (W4404)
Cross-references: - links to VS-07 (store), VS-138 (IFM), VS-24 (HSE), VS-63 (task), W4386 (standards), W4392 (system), W4404 (CAPA)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Checklist-compliance risk**: walk done but hazards missed (tick-box); mitigated by hazard-register-driven checklist + photo evidence
- **Spill-response risk**: wet floor unattended → slip injury (most common claim); mitigated by immediate cone/spill-kit protocol + "wet floor" signage (W4398)
System Touchpoints: - Mobile inspection app vs hazard register (W4392); store-ops task (VS-63); IFM CMMS (VS-138); HSE (VS-24); BI (VS-28)
Time Estimate: - ~20–30 min/inspection × ~216,000/yr ≈ ~72,000–108,000 staff-hrs/yr (built into existing store-staff model)

steps.activity: Store team run the documented safety walk per zone (sales floor, lumber/tile yard, parking) against the hazard register (W4386) — spills, obstacles, damaged racking, blocked egress, exposed sharps, unstable stacks
Store team correct immediate hazards (spill clean-up, cone-off, restack, remove) or escalate to IFM (VS-138)/HSE, and log every finding into the incident system (W4392) including near-misses
Customer Safety/HSE trend findings, identify repeat hazards, and trigger corrective action (W4404) or standard change (W4386)

fields.Participants: Merchandising (VS-55), Store Ops (VS-07), Stock Associates, IFM (VS-138), HSE (VS-24)
fields.Volume: ~5,000 replenishment orders/month + daily restocking across 200 stores

Automation Opportunity: - Safe-stack standards in planogram app; racking-load-capacity register; damage-photo → disposition; racking-integrity PM schedule
Controls: - CTL-672: stacking standards enforced per merchandise type; racking integrity audited; unstable stock quarantined; clear-aisle maintained
Cross-references: - links to VS-55 (planogram), VS-04/VS-05 (inventory), VS-138 (IFM), W4386 (standards), W4389 (design), W4393 (inspection)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Falling-stock injury risk**: unstable cement/tile/lumber/appliance stack collapses on customer → high-severity; mitigated by height/restraint standards, banding, and inspection
- **Racking-failure risk**: damaged/overloaded racking collapses; mitigated by periodic racking-integrity audit & load-capacity labeling
System Touchpoints: - Planogram/space (VS-55); WMS/inventory (VS-04/VS-05); IFM CMMS/racking (VS-138); hazard register (W4386); store task (VS-63)
Time Estimate: - ~5–10 min per replenishment event for safe-stack verification

steps.activity: Stock team apply safe-stacking/pallet/racking standards per merchandise type (cement max-height, tile-palette banding, lumber cribbing/stickers, appliance restraint) per W4389/W4386
Stock team verify clear-aisle width, no overhang into pedestrian aisles, stable endcaps, and blocked/restricted access for unstable loads; quarantine damaged/unstable stock
Merchandising/IFM audit racking integrity (load capacity, damage, anchorage) periodically and on damage; repair/replace unsafe racking

fields.Participants: Store Ops (VS-07), HSE (VS-24), Stock Associates (operators), IFM (VS-138), Contingent (VS-98)
fields.Trigger: Equipment movement in customer-occupied area; replenishment during trading

Automation Opportunity: - Operator-certification gate; equipment pre-use checklist app; geofenced exclusion zones; equipment-incident analytics
Controls: - CTL-672 (ensure controlled execution — In-Store Customer Safety Operations & Hazard Control (PA-147.2).)
- CTL-672: off-hours preference + spotter + exclusion zone + pedestrian-right-of-way; operator certified; equipment pre-use inspected; incidents investigated (W4402)
Cross-references: - links to VS-24 (HSE), VS-138 (IFM), VS-98 (contingent), VS-115 (calibration), W4389 (design), W4401/W4402 (incident)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Equipment-contact fatality/severity risk**: forklift/reach-truck strikes customer in shared aisle → catastrophic; mitigated by off-hours preference, spotter, exclusion zones, pedestrian-right-of-way
- **Uncertified-operator risk**: untrained operator → accident; mitigated by certification gate & pre-use inspection
System Touchpoints: - HSE (VS-24); IFM equipment (VS-138); store task (VS-63); contingent workforce (VS-98); incident (W4392); calibration (VS-115)
Time Estimate: - ~2–5 min pre-use inspection × multiple moves/day; spotter time per move

steps.a: Store Manager / Head of Customer Safety
steps.activity: Store Manager/HSE enforce equipment-in-sales-area rules — preferred off-hours movement, segregated lanes (W4389), reverse-spotter/blue-light/horn, pedestrian-right-of-way, exclusion zones
HSE/Store Ops certify operators (license, refresher), inspect equipment pre-use (horns, lights, brakes, reverse alarms), and remove unsafe equipment from service
HSE/Customer Safety audit adherence, investigate any equipment-customer near-miss/incident (W4401/W4402), and tighten rules on learning

fields.Participants: IFM (VS-138), Store Ops (VS-07), Loss Prevention (VS-23), Security (VS-138/VS-23), Customer Safety

workflows.name: Parking Lot, Exterior & Site-Access Customer Safety

Automation Opportunity: - Lighting-burnout/fixture monitoring; surface-defect photo→work-order; CCTV-coverage map; curbside-zone management (VS-152)
Controls: - CTL-672 (ensure controlled execution — In-Store Customer Safety Operations & Hazard Control (PA-147.2).)
- CTL-672: daily exterior inspection; lighting on at dusk; surface defects corrected; security patrol/CCTV; PM maintained
Cross-references: - links to VS-138 (IFM), VS-23 (LP), VS-152 (parking/curbside), W4386 (standards), W4393 (inspection)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Parking-lot injury risk**: trip on pothole/curb, poor-lighting assault/vehicle-pedestrian → high-frequency claim; mitigated by daily lighting/surface inspection & PM
- **Security risk**: parking-lot crime → customer harm + reputational; mitigated by patrol, CCTV, lighting (links VS-23)
System Touchpoints: - IFM CMMS (VS-138); CCTV (VS-23.2); store-ops (VS-07); loss prevention (VS-23); parking/curbside (VS-152); hazard register (W4386)
Time Estimate: - ~15–20 min daily exterior inspection/site; PM per schedule

steps.activity: IFM/Store inspect parking lot & exterior — lighting coverage/burnouts, crosswalks/striping, potholes, drainage/flood, speed bumps, signage, cart corrals, curbs/wheel-stops — and correct/escalate
Loss Prevention/Security manage parking security (patrol, CCTV coverage, lighting-on-at-dusk, valet/courtesy if offered) and curbside/BOPIS pickup-zone safety (W4528)
IFM maintain exterior civil works (asphalt, line-marking, lighting, drainage) via PM and reactive work orders (VS-138)

workflows.name: Chemical, Paint & Hazmat Customer Exposure Control (In-Store)

Automation Opportunity: - SDS/labeling linked to PIM (VS-137); chemical-area compliance checklist; spill-response workflow; ventilation monitoring
Controls: - CTL-672: chemicals placed per ventilation/containment/separation; SDS accessible; BFP storage limits enforced; spill response ready
Cross-references: - links to VS-24.3 (hazmat), VS-114 (DG), VS-137 (PIM/SDS), VS-138 (ventilation), W4386 (standards), W4401 (response)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Customer-exposure risk**: solvent/thinner/paint exposure (inhalation/skin/eye) → injury/claim; mitigated by ventilation, containment, SDS access, first-aid
- **Fire-load risk**: flammable chemical stock exceeds BFP limits → fire; mitigated by storage-limit control (links VS-24.3/VS-138)
System Touchpoints: - HSE hazmat (VS-24.3); DG (VS-114); PIM/SDS (VS-137); merchandising (VS-01); IFM ventilation (VS-138); incident (W4392)

steps.activity: Merchandising/HSE control customer-accessible chemical placement — ventilation, secondary containment, separation of incompatibles, child-resistant where required, restricted-access for high-hazard, SDS accessibility (links VS-137)
Store team manage in-store chemical spills/exposure (spill kit, ventilation, customer first-aid/eyewash, evacuation if needed), contain, and report (W4401/W4405)

steps.a: HSE Lead / Head of Customer Safety
steps.activity: HSE/DG audit chemical-area compliance (BFP Fire Code storage limits, DENR-EMB, ventilation, labeling) and SDS availability (VS-114/VS-137)

workflows.name: Customer Safety Signage, Wayfinding & Barrier Management

Automation Opportunity: - Signage-standard library linked to hazards; deploy-task auto-trigger; fixed-signage PM & defect tracking
Controls: - CTL-672 (ensure controlled execution — In-Store Customer Safety Operations & Hazard Control (PA-147.2).)
- CTL-672: safety signage standard maintained; immediate deploy on hazard; daily legibility/placement check; fixed signage PM'd
Cross-references: - links to VS-55 (visual merch), VS-14 (signage/print), VS-138 (IFM), W4386 (standards), W4389 (zone design), W4393 (inspection)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Signage-absence risk**: hazard without signage → liability ("should have known"); mitigated by immediate-deploy protocol & daily legibility check
- **Wayfinding-failure risk**: customer enters restricted/hazard zone unknowingly; mitigated by clear wayfinding & barriers
System Touchpoints: - Visual merch/planogram (VS-55); signage/print (VS-14); IFM CMMS (VS-138); store task (VS-63); hazard register (W4386)
Time Estimate: - Per-deploy minutes; daily check folded into W4393

steps.a: Head of Customer Safety / VP Visual Merch
steps.activity: Visual Merch/HSE specify the safety-signage & wayfinding standard — wet-floor, watch-your-step, forklift-in-area, hard-hat-zone (yard), no-climb, emergency-exit, restroom/PWD, chemical-area — per zone (W4389)
Store team deploy signage/barriers immediately on hazard (spill cone, wet-floor sign, caution tape, aisle-closure) and remove when cleared; inspect legibility/placement daily
IFM maintain fixed signage/wayfinding/barriers (exit signs, emergency lighting, handrails, bollards) via PM (VS-138); replace damaged/illegible

Automation Opportunity: - Footfall/people-counting for occupancy; queue-density alerting; event-crowd-plan templates; post-event incident analytics
Controls: - CTL-672 (ensure controlled execution — In-Store Customer Safety Operations & Hazard Control (PA-147.2).)
- CTL-672: peak crowd-management plan per event; entry metering; occupancy cap vs BFP; post-event review
Cross-references: - links to VS-14 (marketing/promo), VS-23 (LP), VS-24 (HSE), VS-28 (footfall), W4391 (BFP compliance), W4402 (investigation), W4404 (CAPA)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Stampede/crush risk**: unmanaged doorbuster crowd → crush/fatality; mitigated by entry metering, stanchions, no-rush culture, occupancy cap
- **Occupancy-exceedance risk**: exceeds BFP assembly-occupancy → fire-safety violation + hazard; mitigated by occupancy monitoring & cap

steps.a: Head of Customer Safety / Marketing Lead

Automation Opportunity: - Accessibility-fixture PM & compliance tracking; assistance-request flow; vulnerable-customer incident analytics
Controls: - CTL-672 (ensure controlled execution — In-Store Customer Safety Operations & Hazard Control (PA-147.2).)
- CTL-672: BP 344 accessibility maintained; assistance provided; vulnerable-customer zones watched; accommodation audited

steps.activity: CX/Customer Safety define vulnerable-customer safety & accommodation — BP 344 accessibility (ramps, aisle width, restroom, parking), priority lane, assistance, child-safety (cart/aisle/chemical/height), senior fall-risk

Store team provide assistance (priority service, carry-out, cart-escort, restroom access), maintain accessible routes/fixtures, and watch for at-risk customers (unaccompanied child, mobility-impaired in yard)
IFM maintain accessibility fixtures (ramps, handrails, accessible restroom, PWD parking) per BP 344/W4389; CX audit accommodation effectiveness (links VS-146)

fields.Frequency: Rare but chain-real event class: ~2–4 vehicle-into-building strikes per year across ~205 roadside sites with parking lots and dock aprons (big-box formats sit behind driving surfaces); most are low-speed parking-lot contacts, the tail case is a high-speed storefront intrusion during trading
fields.Owner: Store Manager (site command); Head of Customer Safety (protocol & reopen gate)
fields.Participants: Regional Manager, Security Guard / Loss Prevention, Facilities & Maintenance (W650 call-out), Structural Engineer (retainer), PNP traffic investigator, third-party insurer (driver's liability desk), VS-26 (property/BI claim, W876), VS-147.3 (injury/claims chain where injuries occur), Store Communications (VS-63), Legal (VS-100 demand & subrogation posture)
fields.Trigger: A motor vehicle strikes a BuildRight building — a storefront or entrance impact, a parking-lot collision with the building face or support columns, a loading-dock/delivery-vehicle impact, or a boom/crane crash against the structure while customers or staff are on site
fields.Volume: 1 event × 1 site × the crash-surface scope (glazing, canopy, columns, racking near the impact line) × the trading-impact tier (partial-zone closure to full closure); each event also opens the driver/third-party liability track and the structural-clearance gate

Automation Opportunity: - Vehicle-impact incident type with a mandatory photo checklist (replaces manual evidence capture)
- Red-tag zone flags that block POS reopening checklists until engineer clearance is recorded
- Claim-pack auto-assembly from the incident record + engineer's report + repair quotes
- Bollard/barrier audit triggers on the site-standards register from the incident record
Background: 'Vehicle into building'/'storefront crash' appear in zero PA files — W330's in-store emergency trigger names structural failure generically but defers event-specific execution, W5555 owns the fatality scene protocol, W1450's structural assessment is quake-specific, and W653 owns our fleet crashing elsewhere — nobody owned the survivable-crash class: the crash-scene safety law (an unstable vehicle, a fuel leak and compromised glazing are hazards before they are evidence), the liability ordering (the driver's compulsory third-party liability and own-damage cover is the primary claim — BuildRight's property loss runs as subrogation, not the other way round), the red-tag structural discipline before any zone reopens (the W5537 BFP-clearance analog for impact damage), and the bollard/barrier retrofit feedback into the site-standards register.
Controls: - CTL-672 (ensure controlled execution — In-Store Customer Safety Operations & Hazard Control (PA-147.2).)

- operational: crash-scene cordons and no-statement rules briefed at every store; red-tag/reopen decisions documented with the engineer's written clearance; subrogation files reconciled to claim outcomes
Pain Points / Risks: - **Structural-understatement risk**: a struck column or canopy beam reads as cosmetic glazing damage; mitigated by Step 3's engineer red-tag before any zone reopens
- **Fault-admission risk**: on-site fault talk by staff becomes the insurer's defense exhibit; mitigated by the no-statement rule and Step 1's PNP investigation ownership
- **Evidence-decay risk**: the vehicle is removed and the scene cleaned before documentation; mitigated by Step 2's preservation hold before any cleanup
- **Recovery-gap risk**: the store sits closed waiting on the third-party insurer; mitigated by Step 5's own-policy BI engagement for the gap period
- **Repeat-impact risk**: the same face is struck again; mitigated by Step 8's bollard/barrier review feeding the retrofit backlog
Staffing Implication: - Absorbed by store management, facilities and the VS-26 claims desk with counsel support; no incremental headcount.
System Touchpoints: - Incident-case record with a vehicle-impact type and mandatory scene-photo attachments
- Facility work orders with a structural flag (links to W650/W47)
- Red-tag/reopen checklist states on the site file
- Claim records to VS-26 (W876) and the third-party subrogation file
- Demand-letter/outside-counsel matter in the legal case system (links to VS-100)
Time Estimate: Per event ≈ 8–20 staff-hours on day one (scene command, evidence, triage) plus 4–8 hours of engineer/insurer follow-through spread over the recovery weeks; at the ~2–4-events-per-year class the chain-wide figure stays under ~100 staff-hours per year, absorbed within store management, facilities and the claims desk.

steps.activity: **Crash-scene safety & command**: hold-back cordon (vehicle instability, fuel leak, glass); isolate power/fuel at the meter where the impact struck utilities; first aid per W501 with injuries routed via W140/VS-147.3; request PNP traffic investigation
**Evidence preservation**: CCTV preservation hold (W838); scene photos before any cleanup; witness details; driver/vehicle/insurer details on the incident record; no fault statements by anyone

**Structural triage**: Facilities + structural-engineer call-out assess the impact zone — glazing, canopy, columns, the racking line behind the face; red-tag zones cordoned; occupancy of unaffected zones documented

**Liability posture**: the driver's CTPL and own-damage insurance is the primary claim track; BuildRight's property loss runs as subrogation; Legal issues the demand/notice letter to driver, owner and insurer
**Claim initiation**: property-claim pack (photos, engineer's report, repair quotes) to the third-party insurer; own-policy engagement (VS-26 W876) for the uninsured gap and business interruption

**Trading-continuity decision**: partial trade behind the cordon is the default; full closure rides the Regional Manager closure authority (the E-02 custody — W2510 decides, W850 executes) when the impact zone touches exits, utilities or occupied selling space; documented either way

**Repair & reopen gate**: repairs under permit where structure is touched; no reopen of red-tagged zones until the structural engineer's written clearance and — where load-bearing elements were struck — the LGU building official's clearance (the W5537 BFP-gate analog)

**After-action & retrofit**: the incident feeds the site-standards register — bollard/barrier adequacy at the struck face reviewed per this PA and VS-138 PM; claims outcome reconciles to the safety-investment backlog
